concepts.def: Angles on a line, around a point, in triangles and parallel lines.
Interior and exterior angles of polygons.
Angle and chord properties of circles.
Identical shapes versus same shape, different size.
Accurate drawings using compasses and a ruler.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A triangle's angles add to 180°.

Quadrilaterals sum to 360°. A regular polygon's interior angle = (n − 2) × 180 ÷ n. Pentagon: 540 ÷ 5 = 108°.

Rectangle: area = length × width. Triangle: area = ½ × base × height.

Circle: area = π r². Perimeter (circumference) = 2π r or πd.

Cuboid: V = l × w × h. Prism: V = cross-section area × length.

Cylinder: V = π r² × h. Cone: V = ⅓ π r² h.

mcqs.q: Angles in a triangle sum to:

options: π × r²
2 × π × r
π × d
½ × π × r²

mcqs.q: Can Pythagoras' theorem be used on any triangle?
options: Yes — it works on any triangle as long as you square the sides.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
No — it only applies to right-angled triangles.
Only on equilateral triangles because all sides are equal.

mcqs.q: In Pythagoras' theorem, which side does c^2 represent?
options: The hypotenuse — the longest side, opposite the right angle.
180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
c^2 represents the side opposite the largest angle that is not 90 degrees.
c^2 represents any side of the triangle as long as the other two are squared.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of any pentagon?
options: 180 degrees, the same as a triangle.
Only on equilateral triangles because all sides are equal.
540 degrees — use (n - 2) x 180 with n = 5.
360 degrees, because all polygons' angles sum to one full turn.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Pythagoras”?
options: a² + b² = c² in a right-angled triangle
Space inside a shape, units²
Angles in a triangle add to 180°
Space taken up by a 3D shape, units³

Total distance around a shape
Angles in a triangle add to 180°
